            Added

            • Plugin Studio › Code: the scripts, and which apps depend on them. Asked: "a plugin looks like two plugins -- that code is a dependency, and it should be under a menu element called Code". A plugin's code is a Script Library script, and since 2026-10-23 every script was also an app, so a plugin with a script drew two rows in Apps and two entries in Plugins. Now a script that a flow app runs (its draft or its published version, read as the app's Dependencies tab reads it) is that app's dependency: the new Code entry of the Explorer lists every script with Used by (the apps that run it, each a link to its Dependencies tab), From package (the plugin package that installed the published version, or written here), status, published version and audience, with Edit, Download the code and Enable / Disable; Import a script and Developer kit moved there. Such a script has no row under Apps, no entry under Plugins, in the Apps-only portal or on Operations › Automation › Scripts. A script no app runs is still an app of its own (runs on its own in Code). The app's Dependencies tab names the section Code it runs and links to Code.
            • Every plugin reads the inventory record and the hardware of the fleet, nothing to publish first. Asked: "Fleet Inventory does not show model, serial number, CPU, RAM, the classification -- it brings nothing". They were reachable only through an administrator dataset the plugin brings, which lands pending until someone publishes it in Administrator › Database › Plugin datasets; on an install where nobody had, every column was empty. The built-in dataset fleet_appliances now also carries device_hostname, model, serial, serial_checked_at, hw_type, ha_mode, ha_vip, is_cluster, last_status, last_checked_at, zone, department, line, tags, maintenance (the first six columns do not move; never a credential), and the new built-in fleet_hardware is the last hardware scan of each device: cpu_count, cpu_model, mem_total_mb, disks_json, raw_json (the output of the scan's read-only commands), source, updated_at. Both are cut to the person who opens the view, like every dataset (a maintenance device only with that permission). Fleet Inventory 2.1.0 reads them.
            • A script writes a data store it declares; data stores and files grow (FA-0016). Asked: "VM inventory must take about 30 MB". A Script Library script that declares store:<slug> among its SATOM data may call store("<slug>").replace(rows): the store becomes exactly rows, every row checked first, one commit, a bad row leaves the old rows. The rows go in chunks of 2 MiB through the run's grant (the same signed, short-lived grant as satom.*, answered on the loopback for the person who runs it) and are staged on the node's disk until the replace; only declared stores, nothing else is writable; a packaged script may declare only a store of its package or of the server. So a data set no longer has to pass through a step (8 MiB). Data stores hold 50,000 rows / 40 MiB (was 20,000 / 16 MiB; measured on a1, 4 GB: 30,000 rows of 28 MB replace in 2.9 s, read in 0.6 s, ~110 MB in the web worker -- 64 MiB was refused because one query of a full store would cost ~800 MB); file fields take 64 MiB (was 32; 20 MiB since 2026-11-13, see Changed).
            • A plugin carries its own code: what a Script Library script may take in and hand back (FA-0016). FA-0016 first put the VM Inventory plugin's logic into SATOM (two steps). The user: "you injected plugin code into SATOM; that can bring problems -- take it out, everything as a plugin". What a plugin's own script needed, and nothing here knows what an inventory is: a script field of type file (the text of the chosen file, up to 32 MiB; a run record keeps only its size) and the same File field in an app's form, passed on by a Run a script step; result() up to 8 MiB (was 256 KiB) -- what one Plugin Studio step keeps; a connection call with max_mb (up to 64 MiB, default 2) that reads like requests(timeout=): the connection's timeout is the wait for each piece, the whole call may take the rest of the script's own time limit. An app package upgrades its own script: a script an earlier version of the SAME package installed, and nobody edited since, gets the package's new files as its next version (it used to be kept forever, so a plugin's new code never arrived); an edited script, or one another package installed, is kept with a warning. store_write mode replace (the rows become exactly a list, checked first, one commit), queries past 5,000 rows and SATOM.onProgress for app views stay -- they are not the plugin's. VM Inventory 1.5.0 is the first plugin built this way: its script reads the inventory API or an imported JSON in any shape (preview first) and the diagram only routes.
            • Every app lists what it depends on (FA-0017). Asked: "in each app put everything it needs, the same as Plugin Studio: data stores, connections, sign-in directories and the API Catalog". Plugin Studio › Apps › app has a Dependencies tab: its Data stores (rows, columns, which other apps share them), Connections (kind, target, whether the secret is set, the API version it is pinned to — also the ones a script step calls), API Catalog versions (status, endpoints), Sign-in directories (the directory each sign-in rule names, on or off), the scripts it runs, the apps it opens, its automations and the apps that run it. Each one links to its page; draft only / published only says which version uses it. What stops the app on this server (a missing store, a connection without its secret, a draft API version, a directory switched off) is listed on top, and the tab's badge turns amber.
            • A plugin upload shows that it is loading, and the install is a job (FA-0017). Asked: "when the plugin is uploaded, show that it is loading — a job would be best — and do it in the background". Import plugin (Plugins) and Import package or bundle (Plugin Studio › Apps) upload with a progress bar (Uploading … 12.4 / 34.5 MB (36 %)), then say Checking the package… until the preview opens; a refusal is shown under the form. Install runs as a job — on the Jobs page and in the dock, named after the file, one line per step: the package read, its signature and rules, each package of a bundle (a refused one in red), everything it created or kept and the secrets stored. An install that takes more than two seconds opens the job's progress page; leave it and the install goes on. It has no Stop: an install writes the database in one go.
            • Runs show what SATOM did and decided (FA-0015). Asked of the restart activities: "these connectivity tests -- did SATOM run them, or who did?". Every step on a run page now says who did it (SATOM, Person or Instructions -- the procedure's text, nothing checked, shown as read instead of ok), where its answer led (yes → 1.2 …), and keeps the output of a ping, traceroute, console or appliance-ping check under Output even when the step saves nothing. A finished run lists Not run on this path: every step it never reached, under the answer that skipped it (1.1 HTTPS answered, so 1.3 Ping, 1.4 SSH … were not run). The steps summary counts the steps SATOM checked itself. Plugin appliance-recovery 1.3.1 says the same in step 1 Connectivity tests.
            • Web Server Manager: the agent can sign in as an account sshd already lets in (SA-0031). A server that lets only some groups in over SSH (AllowGroups ssh-user …) refused satom-mon, and the only fixes were to change that server's sshd or its groups. Install and Reinstall now ask for the Agent account: satom-mon (created by the installer, as before) or the account of the credential that installs it -- sshd already lets that one in, it is signing in at that moment. The installer takes it as --user <account>: it creates nothing, keeps the account's password, shell and other keys, and adds SATOM's key line restricted to satom-webctl exactly as for satom-mon (no shell, no forwarding, only from the SATOM nodes), the two sudo rules and the ACLs for that account. The agent's own backups, log and certificates follow the account. A reinstall onto another account first removes the agent from the one it was on; Remove takes it off the account it is on and never deletes an account the installer did not create; the satom-webctl agent credential follows. The choice is checked on the server side: satom-mon, the installing credential's account or the current one -- never root (also refused by the helper and the installer, by name and by uid 0), never a name the request makes up. The installer's AllowUsers/AllowGroups warning and the job's diagnosis name this way out. The agent job's error is no longer cut at 300 characters mid-sentence (the tester's copy ended in "Found on the"): the job runner cuts every error there, so the agent job records its own, whole -- post-check, installer warnings and diagnosis.

            Changed

            • The API Explorer says why a leaf is unknown. The 159 unknown marks of an 8.0.8 build are 111 by-parent sub-tables the REST sweep never reads, 44 monitor/log endpoints and 4 sub-tables of objects measured absent on 8.0.8. The tally and each badge's tooltip now say so, and a sub-table of an object measured absent is marked absent (8.0.8: absent 5 → 9, unknown 159 → 155).
            • The Build compatibility page refuses nonsense and explains itself. One build says "a comparison needs two builds" and shows that build's own coverage instead of "These builds agree on every field shown". A build the library does not know (b=9.9.9, b=garbage) is an error naming the known builds (HTTP 400); a diff to it no longer reads "+0 / -0" as if nothing changed. More than eight builds names the ones left out, and keeps the fleet's builds first (the default selection was the first eight in library order). A diff of a build with itself is refused with a sentence; format=json answers {"ok": false, "error", "message", "known"} with HTTP 400. In the diff, a field renamed between builds (same CLI attribute id, for example max-setting-initial-window-size to h2-setting-initial-window-size) is listed once, as a rename, instead of also as an unrelated addition and removal, and the GUI block says "N of M pages measured".
            • Fleet objects shows and filters the build. Every row has a Build column (version and build as the device reports it, e.g. 8.0.8 build0140) and a server-side Build filter (also in search mode and in the CSV).
            • Config Compare knows the two boxes may run different builds. Each line shows the source and destination build (and the TSV export carries src_build, dst_build, build_note). A field difference the build diff explains is marked "not on 7.6.8" or "renamed: max-... on 7.6.8 = h2-... on 8.0.8", and an object the other build does not have says "object not on 8.0.6"; a row whose differences are all explained carries a build only badge. The verdict is not changed by the marks.
            • One answer to "does this build have this page", for the menu, the page, the banner and the build diff. Found while reviewing FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.8 side by side: the menu hid a page the build does not have, but opening its address served it with a Create New button, and the build-diff page said "no GUI layout was measured" for a page that was simply removed. All four now read the same page state from the API library of the device's exact build. A page whose object the build was measured not to have (MCP on 7.6.8, File Exception on 8.0.8) is left out of the menu; its address still answers, read-only, with "FortiWeb 7.6.8 does not have this object (measured). The page exists from 8.0.6 on." (or "was removed after 7.6.8"), no Create New, no Save and no "+ Create" from a selector. An object the library never measured on the build stays in the menu and says "Not measured on this build yet". The build-diff note names which of the two cases it is.
            • A page the device shows under two names appears once. Let's Encrypt and ACME, Mobile API, OCSP and the Not in GUI copy of Web Anti-Defacement edit the same object across builds; a device's menu lists the page whose layout was measured closest to its build, found from the layouts' own endpoints, not from a list of names.
            • One sentence says where a layout comes from, everywhere. The page banner, the dialogs, the Not in GUI, but in CLI sections, the Not in GUI device page and the exception forms all print Layout measured on FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116 · this device runs 8.0.8 build0140 · same train, with a badge (same build, same version, same train, older or newer train, firmware not known) and both builds zero padded as the device reports them. Layouts from an older or newer train, and a device whose firmware is unknown, used to get an empty note; the Not in GUI page used to say "(exact)" for a layout of another build. The device page now says "every field of the exact build" only when that build's CLI tree is measured, and otherwise names what the build is measured on.
            • A dropdown no longer turns into a text box when the layout of another build lost its choices. Select, radio and checkbox-list controls without a list take it from the device's own build in the API library (the CLI tree prints every option); failing that from the same field in the nearest other layout, marked options from 7.6.8, not verified on 8.0.8; only with neither is it a text box marked choices not measured. On the lab FortiWeb pair this took the controls that fell back to text from 72 (7.6.8) and 107 (8.0.8) to 14 and 20.
            • Fields the build lacks are marked when the layout is from another build. A field the library says the build does not have is drawn disabled with not on 8.0.8 (renamed to h2-setting-initial-window-size) when the rename is known; a field the build was never measured on keeps working and says not measured on 8.0.8. Display only: what Save sends is decided by the build check.
            • A failed read shows the device's answer. A settings form whose live read fails prints the HTTP status, the errcode and the message the device returned (for example HTTP 500, errcode -20001, The REST API has invalid URL) and says whether the device was unreachable, the library says the build does not serve the object, or the device refused the read, instead of "the device did not answer".
            • FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled. A row registered in the root ADOM of a device whose system global has adom-admin enable now says so under its empty lists and in Capacity (ADOMs are enabled on this device: this row shows the root ADOM only ... register the device again with ADOM (vdom) set to the ADOM's name) instead of "a configuration sync fills the SATOM cache" and "In use 0 / 50" for a box holding 50 server policies in another ADOM.
            • File fields take up to 20 MiB, and the app run route takes them. Asked: "files must be up to 20 MB". A File field promised 64 MiB, but /apps/<slug>/run -- where a plugin view's SATOM.call / SATOM.submit and the app's own run page send it -- refused every body over 1 MiB (measured on a1 through nginx: 2 MiB → 413), so a file of 2 MB never reached the app. Now one number, 20 MiB, for the flow apps' and the scripts' File fields and for the browsers that read the file, and the run route takes a body sized for it (twice the file, as JSON grows it, plus the form: 41 MiB) only for an app whose form has a File field; every other app and every other /apps route keeps 1 MiB. Over that, the 413 says (a file is at most 20 MiB); a longer file inside it is refused by the field with the same number. A 30,000-VM inventory export (~34 MB) no longer fits one file field: 20 MiB is the operator's limit (2026-11-13).
            • The app editor names the installed plugin version. The header read v4 published on DNS Lookup, which looked like the plugin version (2.0.1 on the downloads hub). It now shows package 2.0.1 for an imported app and SATOM's own publish counter as #4 published (also in the Publish card).
            • Plugin Studio shows what Report Studio has. Under the app list, Plugin Studio › Apps draws Report Studio's Custom views and Code plugins tables, the same ones (one template each), for every ADOM the administrator may enter, with an ADOM column; Open, View, Download, Disable and Delete act in the view's own ADOM. Only for someone who holds Report Studio. Report Studio itself is unchanged.
            • Every plugin page names the installed version. The Plugin Studio app list still read v4 (the publish counter) and the pages an operator opens said nothing. Plugin Studio › Apps has a Version column (the package version, authored here for an app built here) and shows the counter as #N; the app's form and view pages, the Custom Views cards and an opened custom view show the package version next to the name.
            • A non-author sees what a runbook check found (FA-0015). The run page hid every step's detail from someone who is not a Plugin Studio author (finding 2026-10-20). The sentence of a runbook check (HTTPS, TCP, ping, traceroute, login, power state, notify, incident…) is written for the person working the procedure and is now shown to them, with the ping / traceroute output; a console command's output and the detail of general steps stay with the authors.
            • Session login works with JSON-only token APIs (FA-0016). A form that the login path refuses with 400, 401, 403, 415 or 422 is sent again as JSON (before: only 415/422), and the shape that worked is remembered until the connection is saved, so a wrong password costs one attempt per login. The token is found in access_token, token, accessToken, jwt or id_token, at the top level or under data/result/response (before: only a top-level access_token). A one-word plain-text answer also counts as the token; an HTML page does not. When the answer sets cookies and carries a token, both are sent; before, any cookie (a load balancer's persistence cookie, say) silently dropped the bearer.

            Security

            • No real network address in the documentation, the form hints or the tests. The safeguards article named the workstation address behind an Attack Search change, and the appliance form suggested a common private-LAN address as its placeholder. The article now says "a customer workstation", the form asks for an IP address or hostname (in all five languages), and the tests that need a private address use one reserved for the purpose. Every published copy of this project goes through a deny-by-default address guard; this release is the first one that passes it.
            • An administrator dataset over the fleet is cut to the person viewing. Found while building the Fleet Inventory plugin (a view over appliances joined to the hardware scan): a published dataset whose rows ARE appliances (appliances as base or join) has no appliance_id column, so it reached every viewer whole -- a maintenance device included for a profile that may not see one. Its rows are now cut by appliances.id, which SATOM adds to the query when the author did not pick it and drops again before the view sees the row. A grouped or aggregated query is left as it was (a row is no longer one appliance). Test: test_an_admin_dataset_over_the_appliances_is_cut_to_the_viewer.
            • SATOM refuses to start in production without FERNET_KEY. Until now a missing key never stopped start-up: app/config.py generated a random key in memory, so the refusal meant to catch it never ran and FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY had no effect. Every gunicorn worker, the scheduler and the reconciler then encrypted with a different key, logged nothing, and a device credential saved by one process could not be read by the others or after a restart. Now, with FLASK_ENV=production, the web app, the scheduler and the reconciler stop at boot with RuntimeError: FERNET_KEY is not set (process: …). Every encrypt and decrypt runs the same check. FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY=1 still starts a throwaway node on a temporary key and logs a WARNING once per process. Development and testing start on a temporary key and log a WARNING. A key set in the environment is used unchanged. Importing the package still never fails, so CLI commands that do not touch encrypted data keep working. A command started as python -m app.… that loads .env through wsgi.py (app.cli_sentinel) used to keep the random key and the SQLite fallback that the earlier import of app.config had filled in. It now reads the key and the database from .env. Before upgrading a node, check that /opt/satom/.env has FERNET_KEY and that it is the same on both HA nodes.
            • The same rule for SECRET_KEY. A missing SECRET_KEY was also replaced by a random key in every process, so each gunicorn worker signed sessions, CSRF tokens, password-reset links and 2FA recovery tokens with its own key. Users were logged out at random and forms failed as "expired" after every restart, with nothing in the log. In production the web app, the scheduler and the reconciler now stop at boot with RuntimeError: SECRET_KEY is not set (process: …). The switch is its own, FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_SECRET_KEY=1 (one WARNING per process), so allowing a throwaway session key never allows a throwaway credential key, and the reverse. Development and testing warn once. A key set in the environment is used unchanged. .env must have the same SECRET_KEY on both HA nodes.

            Documentation

            • Stale documents corrected against the code. Writing the four project documents showed older ones that contradicted the code; every occurrence is now fixed. What happens without FERNET_KEY is described as it now behaves (see Security; overview.md, engineering.md, Docs Center configuration-files, security-model, error-messages, troubleshooting). The manager runs as a primary with a standby and manual failover (management-overview.md). Tests never run on a node: targeted runs and the nightly suite (about 24,000 tests, roughly 100 minutes) run on the audit runner (engineering.md §10, README.md, CLAUDE.md, testing-guide.md, implementation-plan.md). A release runs its version, CHANGELOG and docs guards; the full suite only with with_suite (release-pipeline.md, Docs Center internal-release-pipeline). Menu paths: the Automation entry is Scheduler, Monitoring has Device health and SATOM health as direct entries with no Fleet health sub-menu, and the Audit Log link sits only in the Administrator group while /audit/ is open to every audit.view holder (user-guide.md and 15 Docs Center articles).
            • Four project documents: technical requirements, app flow, testing guide, implementation plan. Requested: the four standard project documents, in Markdown and in the Documentation Center. Technical requirements (docs/technical-requirements.md, Docs Center technical-requirements): what SATOM must do, capabilities by area with their permissions, supported products, platform/runtime stack, sizing, ports, security, availability and the non-functional rules. App flow (docs/app-flow.md, Docs Center app-flow): sign-in to first screen, the screen map, core journeys as flows, what changes by role, where long operations go. Testing guide (docs/testing-guide.md) and Implementation plan (docs/implementation-plan.md, with the plan register and the open work): internal, in the Docs Center's internal category only. Not added to the node manual (publication is opt-in).
            • The rules have one home: Design system and Product rules. Requested: the stylesheets, colours and rules documented and organised, in the documentation as well. Two new documents, published in the manual (Build & integrate) and the Documentation Center: Design system (docs/design-system.md — which stylesheet owns what, every colour token and status badge with its measured contrast, the components to reuse, card grids, charts, CSP constraints, plugin views and a checklist) and Product rules (docs/product-rules.md — device writes in six steps, HTTP 200 is not success, every field visible, Settings vs Operations, plugins vs basic elements, Plugin Studio, menu folders, English only). CLAUDE.md points at both and loses its 2026-07 append log (in git history). Theming: the "known debt" note described the pre-1.2.3 orange palette as the shipped one; it now says Aurora is AA-clean.

            Tests

            • test_sandbox_start.py (new): the two runner units carry no ProtectKernelTunables=/ProtectProc=/ProtectKernelLogs= and keep the rest of their containment; only bwrap's own refusal (exit 1, a single bwrap: line) is reported as a sandbox that did not start; the runner's record clears on the next run that starts; the System packages card shows a runner's refusal and ignores the peer's record copied by the HA data sync.
            • test_public_docs: the four manuals e7a77747 keeps out of the published manual on purpose (app-flow, implementation-plan, technical-requirements, testing-guide) are named in doc_publication.INTERNAL_DOCS -- the guard had been red since -- and no published manual may link one (the overview and engineering pages named the testing guide as a link the publisher turned into text; now text).
            • test_studio_script_connections: a run whose declared connection cannot be handed over is queued with the reason and no secret (test_the_queued_request_never_holds_a_connection_secret, test_one_unavailable_connection_does_not_stop_the_others), the runner hands it to the broker with the reason (test_the_runner_hands_an_unavailable_connection_with_its_reason), and the broker answers it without dialling (test_broker_answers_an_unavailable_connection_with_the_reason).
            • A script's store write (FA-0016). tests/test_studio_pipes.py: the limits fit a 30 MB inventory; store:<slug> is a valid declaration and a bad slug is not; a declared store is replaced in chunks in one commit and the stage is removed; a bad row writes nothing; first starts the stage over; another store, a forged grant, a missing store and an unknown action are refused; the stage is capped; the SDK chunks, then replaces, and aborts the stage when a call fails. tests/test_app_package_scripts.py: a packaged script may write only a store of the package or of the server. 7 mutations bite.
            • SATOM no longer keeps or tests other plugins' builds. The user, after the VM Inventory code left SATOM: "take the old plugins out too". Removed: the signed builds of DNS & LB Lookup (dns-records, dns-decommission, dns-lb-lookup), SOC Search, the six Troubleshooting plugins and the Web Server Manager bundle with its 13 apps from tests/fixtures/plugins/, the two files that only tested them (test_dns_plugin_view.py, test_soc_search_plugin.py) and the 11 tests elsewhere that imported them. The 53 tests of those files that pin SATOM itself stay (the menus, the pages answering by URL, the permissions and the steps those plugins are built from). plugin-hello and fleet-inventory stay: they are not product plugins but the samples that prove SATOM's package reader and the generator agree on the format and the signature. A plugin's tests live with the plugin now.
            • Generic pipes, and the plugin's code out (FA-0016). tests/test_studio_pipes.py (was test_studio_api_search.py, the plugin's tests removed): session login to a JSON token API, replace, queries past 5,000 rows, an HTTP call with a deadline reading an answer that keeps arriving, app and script file fields (megabytes in, only the size kept), the 8 MiB script result, a script call with max_mb (refused without it past 2 MiB, bad values refused, the rest of the script's time as deadline), and that the removed steps are gone. tests/test_app_package_scripts.py: an upgrade publishes the new files of the script the package installed; an edited one and another package's are kept. tests/test_vm_inventory_plugin.py and its fixtures are gone: the plugin tests itself (plugins/vm-inventory/tests in satom-plugins).
            • Dependencies tab and the install job (FA-0017). tests/test_studio_app_deps.py: names are read from the draft and the published version (diagram, actions, form, view context steps and uses), each says where; a connection a script calls is listed via the script; problems name a missing store, a connection without its secret and a directory switched off, and a secret value never reaches the list; the editor draws a row per object linked to its page. tests/test_plugin_import_job.py: the upload answers JSON to the uploader and keeps the redirect for a plain post; Install is the only plugins route wrapped as a job, kept in the ledger when fast, with no Stop and the file in its title; a slow install lands on the wait page (package footnote) and replays the editor redirect; a refused bundle member is a failed step. A signed-by label bug was caught here (an unsigned package read signed by none).
            • Bootstrap before a view's inline scripts. tests/test_studio_view.py (test_bootstrap_is_there_before_the_views_inline_scripts): the frame document loads Bootstrap in the head, before the view's body; the data island, the bridge and the view's script stay after the body, in that order.
            • Report Studio inside Plugin Studio. tests/test_studio_report_studio.py (new): the views of every ADOM with ADOM, package and links in their ADOM; Report Studio has no ADOM column and no _adom=None; a script-library author without Report Studio does not get the section.
            • App editor header. tests/test_studio_app_header.py (new): an imported app shows its package version and the publish counter as #N, never vN; an app built in SATOM has no package badge. Also: the Apps list has a Version column and no vN, the operator page of an imported app and the Custom Views card and page carry the package version.
            • What a run shows of its decisions (FA-0015). tests/test_studio_run_path.py (new): who did each step, where a two-arrow step's answer led, the steps a finished run skipped under the answer that skipped them (a step walked later is not listed; a waiting run claims nothing), the raw output kept on the step by the walk, and what a non-author sees (check results and ping / traceroute output, never a console dump nor a general step's detail).
            • FERNET_KEY start-up policy. tests/test_fernet_key_policy.py (new): production refuses an invented key or no key, naming the variable; FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY=1 starts with exactly one WARNING (a falsy value does not); development/testing warn once; a real key is used unchanged with no log; encrypt() and the models' cipher refuse in production too. In a fresh interpreter: create_app(), the scheduler and the reconciler exit non-zero without the key; the override starts and warns once; and wsgi.py loading .env after app.config was imported gets the key and the database from the file. tests/test_route_audit.py: the production .env fixture carries a FERNET_KEY, as every real one does.
            • SECRET_KEY start-up policy. tests/test_secret_key_policy.py (new): the same cases as the FERNET_KEY policy, plus: the FERNET override does not open the SECRET_KEY gate, and the start-up check runs both gates (a real FERNET_KEY does not let a missing SECRET_KEY through). The FERNET_KEY fresh-interpreter tests now give the process a real SECRET_KEY, so each file tests one gate, and the late-.env test also checks SECRET_KEY. The route-audit production fixture carries both keys.
            • The WAF export accent is checked against the screen. test_the_export_palette_is_the_same_one_the_screen_draws used to skip the accent without saying so: waf.js reads --fw-accent at run time, and its pattern only matched literals. It now reads the waf.js fallback and the fortiweb.css token, and the export has to match both.
            • The plain-text template bomb is 10 MB again (test_studio_security). It was 2.5 MB, legal since the app views raised the value limit to 8 MiB (a4dc9689), so it had been red in every nightly.

            • SOC Search is read-only, and a test says so. Requested: the SOC Search plugin (satom-plugins soc-search) without the DNS Records dialog, so it only reads. soc-search 1.1.0 has no DNS Records (header button, pencil per entry, dialog), no SPO Regex save (rules can be tried, not changed), and its view uses no other app, so it imports without dns-records. The signed package is a fixture (tests/fixtures/plugins/soc-search-1.1.0.satomplugin) and tests/test_soc_search_plugin.py checks it: it imports alone, every diagram step only reads, the view draws no write control even for a user who may write everything on the DNS Lookup page, dns-records cannot be run through it, and spo_save is refused (400).

            • Five nightly guards were red on main; green again. test_advisor_stream read the bookmarks rail's script instead of the Scout page's (it took the largest inline script of the document, and the rail's outgrew the page's when drag-to-reorder landed); it now takes the largest one inside the page content (<main id="fw-main">). test_nav_admin_sections knows the API section of Administrator (2026-11-09). test_chrome_reachability checked the old per-ADOM bookmarks panel; the panel is general since 2026-11-08, so it now pins what must still hold: a reader confined to some ADOMs never sees a device or a bookmark of another one, not even their own, with the unconfined reader as the control. test_tool_modal_chrome: the Migrate into page and two Appliance buttons used the reversed fw-btn-* spelling the guard freezes; they use btn-fw-*.

            Fixed

            • API Explorer: the CLI evidence statement is decided in one place. A build whose CLI schema comes from an imported knowledge pack now reads "CLI schema of 8.0.8 from the knowledge pack ...; no local dump of this build was captured" instead of the legacy "no usable CLI dump has been captured" sentence; that sentence appears only when the build has no evidence of either kind.
            • API Explorer: the page opens on the appliance named in ?appliance_id= (the picker used to read ?id= and default to another appliance, so the Build card described the wrong one).
            • A sub-table row dialog with no title of its own is named by the table that opens it ("URL Encryption Rule › Exceptions row") on every surface, including the removed and added dialogs of the build diff, instead of a humanised template id.
            • An import dialog (Sign CA, Scanner File Import) is no longer drawn as a Create form: its fields are read-only, there is no Save and no "creates the object", and one sentence says the import is done on the device (with a link to SATOM's own certificate import where there is one). Both import dialogs go through the same code.
            • A settings form offers Save only over an object that was read and that SATOM may write; an empty answer is never a base for a blind body, and the Save route refuses it too. A GUI API form is no longer told "the API library could not be read", and a boolean shows on an enable / disable radio (Automatic Patch Upgrades now shows the device's value).
            • A device-managed tab (Firmware) and a monitor tab (ML detail tabs) draw one sentence instead of an empty grid, with a link to the Upgrade Flow on Firmware.
            • Dialog titles never fall back to a raw template id: the template's title, then the entry that opens the dialog, then the page's menu label with (new) / (edit), then the id as words; the build diff uses the same function and lists added / removed objects one per line.
            • The origin line of a page the build does not have says "not on this build" instead of a train warning.
            • The API Explorer CLI evidence card shows the capture (or knowledge pack digest) of the selected appliance's own build, and names the neighbour build when it has to show one.
            • A caption repeated by the layout ("Name" twice) and a table headed by its own section title are drawn once.
            • Grid sentences wrap. The empty-list sentence of a grid (the ADOM notice is ~300 characters) was one nowrap line, clipped at 1440 px and cut at 390 px. A cell that holds a sentence wraps; the empty state takes the width of its card.
            • One wording for a failed read, every product. FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator pages no longer print " did not answer: device refused: Invalid VM License". New services/gui_read_error.py reads the client's error text back into FortiWeb's three-way wording: is unreachable, does not serve this object over REST, refused the read: HTTP 200, Invalid VM License (status, code and message of the device's own answer). _read_form_object uses the same helper.
            • Renamed-object redirect. An object that carries one title on both builds (OCSP, Mobile API Protection) no longer says "OCSP" is called "OCSP": the flash says the address is the other build's name for it.
            • A page the build does not have says so once. No "older/newer train, some fields" warning above the statement and no second copy of it in the empty list.
            • Build compatibility, GUI layout. A page that is one object under two names (Let's Encrypt / ACME, OCSP, Mobile API Protection) is compared as one page under both names instead of "the object exists on 7.6.8 but no GUI layout was measured there"; changed dialogs are named by the template's title (the id is the small text and the tooltip) and never printed as x -> x.
            • Marks only where they belong. "choices not measured" only on a choice control that has a field; a control the layout draws with no field says "not bound to a field". A keyless choice control that duplicates a toggle of the same label (FortiGate Security Fabric role) is drawn once. A tab with no caption takes the title of the dialog it opens (FortiClient EMS Settings instead of "Fctems").
            • Not in GUI device page. The 150 objects whose every REST field the GUI shows are one expandable line instead of 150 cards saying "(0)".
            • List columns bound to nothing. A column the rows do not carry (FortiWeb 8.0.8 Network > Interface: IPv4, IPv4 Access Options, Status, Link Status) is marked "not bound" on the header with a tooltip and its cells read "n/a" instead of looking like "no IP address".
            • Fleet objects. The Build column stays on one line.
            • Contrast. Bootstrap defaults that leaked past the product tokens are mapped to them in fortiweb.css: code, .text-muted, link / nav-tab / outline-primary blue, danger / success text, outline-secondary and outline-info buttons (all >= 4.5:1).
            • Catalogues. 129 untranslated msgids appended to the es, de, fr and it catalogues; tests/test_catalog_coverage.py is green again.
            • Caches built from imported knowledge follow it in every process. The vendor-doc field overlay (fortiweb_field_schema), the object editor's allow-list and sub-table index (objform) and the Web Protection menu (wp_menu) were memoised for the life of each process and cleared, at best, in the process that ran the import or the registry edit; every other web worker and the scheduler kept the old view until a restart. The overlay is keyed by the file's mtime and size; the registry-derived views are keyed on the registry loader's own maps and rebuild within its 60 s window.
            • The HTTP Protocol Constraints table says what the build lacks. When the layout comes from another build, a constraint the device's build does not have is drawn disabled with not on 8.0.8 (renamed to h2-setting-initial-window-size-check), and one nobody measured says not measured on 8.0.8, like every other dialog.
            • A measured exception row dialog that lacks keys no longer hides them. The 8.0.8 HTTP Header Security exception dialog carries one field of four; the form drew one input. The keys the device schema names are now drawn in a last block Not in this layout (REST fields). An exception form for an object the build does not have (File Exception on 8.0.x) carries the page's does not have this object (measured) sentence.
            • Selects fed by another collection are reference selectors. HA SDN Connector, a pool member's SDN Connector and Site Publish's RADIUS Server (typed <datasource> in the build's CLI tree) were text boxes; they now list system/sdn-connector / user/radius-user. The 8.0.8 Content Routing match dialog, whose layout names the policy instead of its match list, takes its five choice lists from the match-list table. Controls still drawn as text boxes (neither the layout nor the CLI tree has the choices): 7 on a 7.6.8 device, 8 on an 8.0.8 one (was 10 and 16).
            • The older name of a renamed object no longer offers a second editor. fwgui/ocsp, letsencrypt, mobileapi and not-in-gui-wad on a device whose menu shows ocsp-certificate, acme, mobile-api, wad (and the reverse on 7.6.8) redirect to the page of the device's own build, with a sentence. Writes are untouched.
            • Build compatibility: one verdict per field, and the preview no longer contradicts itself. A field the target build does not have used to be reported twice: "will be skipped" and, in the next line, "not shown by the FortiWeb GUI ... SATOM still writes it". It now gets the skip line only; the same holds for CLI-only, invalid-value, out-of-range and absent-object fields. The wording is fixed too: "was never measured" for one field ("were" for several), and a check with a single target no longer ends every sentence with "(1 appliance)".
            • A build whose fields nobody read is never "fits". The template compatibility matrix, the template's bindings, its list badge and Mass Deploy's Fit column said "fits, warnings" for a build that serves the objects but has no field evidence. They now say served, fields not measured. Mass Deploy's Fit column also printed the raw cell key ("ok") and never turned green; it now reads fits / fits, warnings / adapt / unmeasured / blocked like the matrix.
            • Fields measured under the CLI key are no longer hidden by an empty registry-name sweep. On an ADOM-enabled FortiWeb (8.0.8) the sweep of the empty root ADOM filed each object under its registry name with no fields, while the harvested schema under the URN key had all of them. The API Explorer showed "blind, 0 fields" for http_protocol, server_policy and server_pool, and the template checks called the build "fits, warnings" while the template carried fields 8.0.8 does not have. Both now read the object under both names (same build only), so the Explorer lists 664 / 245 / 38 fields and the templates show their real verdict (adapt).
            • The API Explorer says "measured" only for a build with a CLI schema and a REST sweep. One channel reads "partially measured (REST sweep only, no CLI schema)" or "(CLI schema only, no REST sweep)".
            • WAF exception forms follow the layouts you import. The index that maps an exception type to the FortiWeb row dialog was cached per firmware string for the life of each process and nothing cleared it, so after a knowledge-pack import every web worker and the scheduler kept the old answer until a restart. It is now keyed on a fingerprint of the template files and rebuilds by itself, in every process.
            • The device GUI notes were drawn in a text colour no stylesheet defines, and the "firmware not read" branch used a Bootstrap warning text colour on white; they now use the design-system tokens and badges.
            • Scripts and integration hooks start on VMs whose kernel refused the sandbox's /proc (FA-0016). Reported on a SLES 15 VM: "exited with code 1 bwrap: Can't mount proc on /newroot/proc: Operation not permitted". The systemd units of the two runners (satom-scripts.service, satom-integrations.service) put read-only mounts over parts of /proc (ProtectKernelTunables=, ProtectProc=), and a kernel only lets the sandbox mount its own /proc where an uncovered one is visible. Both directives are gone from those two units; the sandbox's private process namespace and /proc, which keep operator code away from every other process, are unchanged. An LXC with nesting did not show the problem, which is why it was not seen on our nodes.
            • A sandbox that does not start says so. A run that bwrap refused ended as "exited with code 1", as if the script had failed. It now ends with "sandbox did not start on this node, so the code never ran: ".
            • System packages no longer says "ok" when the runners cannot start the sandbox. The card's check runs in the web service, whose systemd unit is not the runners'. Each runner now records whether its last sandbox started (data/scripts/ and data/integrations/, sandbox-health.json, per node), and the card shows installed, not usable with the runner's reason until a later run starts.
            • A script whose connection SATOM cannot hand over still runs (FA-0016). Reported: "not started: connection vm-inventory-api has a secret and a script receives connection secrets only from the vault -- but I only want to import or preview a file". A Script Library run was refused before it started when ANY connection it declares could not be handed over (no secret saved, no vault, the vault refused), even when that run never calls it. Now the run starts and every call to that connection answers the reason (a ConnectionError in the script); the other connections and the rest of the script work. A connection that does not exist still refuses the run. VM Inventory's Import JSON and preview work without the API's connection; its sync still needs it.
            • A plugin view's script can use Bootstrap while the page loads. The view frame loaded Bootstrap's script after the view's body, so an inline script that built a dialog at load (new bootstrap.Modal(...)) threw and stopped: in the DNS Lookup plugin the DNS Records and Delete dialogs (and the Edit-in-a-new-window links) did nothing. Bootstrap now loads in the frame's head. The plugin itself is fixed too (dns-lb-lookup 2.0.3 builds its dialogs on first use), so it works on SATOM versions without this fix.
            • A data-store query no longer stops at 5,000 rows. A store holds 20,000 rows, but a query (a view's context, Read a data store, an update or a delete by match) silently worked on the first 5,000: a VM inventory of 6,000 would have shown, matched and deleted only part of itself. It now returns as many rows as the store holds (the bytes are still capped at 16 MiB a store); the store page still draws the first 5,000.
            • A connection's secret box says what to type (FA-0016). The tester read the VM Inventory connection's secret as "type the API token", but a Session login signs in with a PASSWORD and uses the token the API answers. The package import preview, the connection page and the publish problem ("connection … has no secret yet") now name the secret by kind and authentication: password (Session login, Basic, PostgreSQL), bearer token, API key, OAuth2 client secret or SSH key, with the user it belongs to.
            • The Builder could not check any plugin (HTTP 500 on /api/v1/builder/rules-pack and /api/v1/builder/target). The FERNET_KEY start-up policy of this version made app/services/encryption.py import app.config by its absolute name; the rules pack carries only modules that import each other relatively, so building it failed and both endpoints answered 500 (satom_plugin.py check, the Builder's Check against SATOM). The import is relative again; tests/test_rules_pack.py was the guard that turned red.
            • Web Server Manager: an agent install that sshd still refuses says why (SA-0030). Reported: "installed, but … still refuses SATOM's key for satom-mon" with Install failed next to it, while the operator's own account signed in fine. The message named five possible causes and none was checked. Now the step says Installer ran and the job asks the server, read-only and as root with the same credential, why sshd refuses the key: sshd's settings for satom-mon from SATOM's address (sshd -T -C, so Match blocks count: AllowUsers/DenyUsers/AllowGroups/DenyGroups, PubkeyAuthentication, AuthenticationMethods, accepted key types), where sshd reads keys and whether SATOM's line is there, StrictModes, the SELinux label, a locked password under UsePAM no, an expired account or aged-out password, a nologin shell, pam_access, and sshd's own log lines. The failure and the agent badge list what it found. The installer fixes what is its to fix: the account it creates gets the password * (sshd treats ! as locked under UsePAM no) and no password ageing, an account it did not create is no longer locked, the key line is added to authorized_keys instead of replacing the file (other keys of an existing account were lost), the key also goes where AuthorizedKeysFile points, the account's .ssh is labelled ssh_home_t on SELinux, and its warnings use sshd's settings for satom-mon (Match blocks were missed). An sshd that refuses Ed25519 keys (FIPS mode, a crypto policy) gets an ECDSA P-256 key and a second install in the same job. A key that sshd accepts only as a first step (AuthenticationMethods publickey,password) is a refusal now; before, the post-check called it "the check could not run" and recorded the agent as installed. Found while testing it live: Remove right after an install or a reinstall left the account satom-mon behind, because SATOM's own sign-in kept a systemd user manager running for a few seconds and the account removal failed without a word. The installer now closes the account's sessions, tries again for ten seconds and says why if it still cannot. The agent badge keeps the whole diagnosis (it was cut at 400 characters, which lost sshd's own line).
            • The migration and page-plugin screens were in English for every language. The device-to-device migration page, the page-plugin screens of Plugin Studio, the notes about converted restores and the Scheduler menu entry added 142 UI strings with no Spanish, German, French or Italian translation. They are now translated in all four, with the same placeholders and markup as the English.
            • The Fleet WAF export drew its accent in the old orange. The PDF rule and the accent chart series still used #EF5424 (SATOM Classic). The page uses the theme accent, Aurora blue #0A3F9F, and the export now does too.
            • The old orange accent leaked into the blue theme. Stylesheets and templates still painted #EF5424 (the pre-1.2.3 accent) as a var() fallback or a literal in about twenty rules — calendar "today", job and appliance progress bars, the update spinner, Registry section buttons, Plugin Studio, the certificate import card, Sentinel overview, the Wiki comment highlight. They now use --fw-accent, so they follow the active theme. SVG and canvas drawings that cannot read a token keep the literal for now (listed in Design system §3).
            • No more orange in drawings, no more dark panels. The Sentinel diagrams and incident timeline, the ER diagram, the process editor, the WAF charts and the monitoring history chart drew the old orange literally; they now take the accent from the active theme (SVG through style, canvas by reading --fw-accent at run time). The ER diagram's "WAF desired-state" domain keeps an orange of its own (#C2410C), readable on white. Four dark panels on a light console are now light: the audit detail drawer, the Switch device picker, the baseline template viewer (its source stays a dark code block) and the Architecture empty state; the High Availability node cards (role pills on the badge palette) and their "this node" pill too. The two map canvases (Architecture, Network Architecture) were converted too — see the next entry.
            • Service Diagram and Network Architecture draw on the light theme. Requested after the design rules were written down: the two map canvases were the last dark "neon" surfaces. They now draw on a light canvas with a faint grid, white nodes and theme text; lines, states and zones use the 600/700 step of each hue so they read on white (zone pills keep white text at 4.9:1 or better, and the device picker uses the same zone colours). Two old defects the dark canvas hid: a #mapSvg text rule outranked every per-class text colour and the chips' colours, so zone labels, hosts, shields and coloured chips all drew in one colour; and the zone pill was sized without its "ZONE · " prefix, so the label ran past it. Both fixed.
            • Plugin views: Search did nothing. In a plugin with its own view (DNS Lookup, SOC Search) the Search button sent nothing: the view's frame was sandboxed without allow-forms, and the browser then blocks a form before its submit event, so the bridge never ran the app. The frame now allows forms (iframe and its Content-Security-Policy); a form still cannot leave the frame (form-action 'none', and the bridge cancels the submission).
            • Operations › Incidents bounced to the ADOM home in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate consoles: every ADOM drew the entry, but the product gate allowed its page in none of those four (tests/test_adom_menu_reachability.py had been red since the page shipped). It opens there now and lists the incidents of that ADOM's devices and those tied to no device.
